name: New York

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt, but candy, soft drinks, fruit drinks under 70% juice and bottled water are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.
Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the general rate, with the excise tax included in the price the sales tax applies to.
Household supplies: diapers are exempt (since December 1, 2022), which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: menstrual products are exempt (since September 1, 2016), which is not taken out here.

Barber, beauty, nail, massage, tanning and similar services are not taxed, except in New York City, which taxes them at 4.5% (counted there); the city also taxes gyms and health salons at 4.5%, not shown here since fitness has no tax figures.

Clothing and footwear under $110 an item are exempt from the 4% state tax, and from local tax in New York City and ten counties (the local rates table). Jewelry and watches are taxed at any price and counted for the state's 4% on their share of US sales of clothing, shoes and jewelry (13%, 2022 Economic Census), 0.52% of what is spent on clothing, shoes and jewelry; the category's rate also takes in laundry and dry cleaning, at their own rate. Where clothing is exempt from local tax, the local tax on jewelry and watches is counted on the same share. Not counted, since no official figure gives their share: items of $110 or more and other taxed accessories.
Laundry and dry cleaning: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Gasoline: the 4% state tax is levied as 8 cents a gallon, shown as 1.78% of an average New York pump price of $4.49; local rates on fuel are set separately (the local rates table). The excise taxes, left out here, come to 23.85 cents a gallon in 2026 (8.05 cents motor fuel tax and testing fee, 15.8 cents petroleum business tax); no 2026 gas tax holiday was enacted.
Auto repair labor: taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Vapor products carry a 20% supplemental sales tax at retail on top of the regular sales tax, which isn't counted here: it falls only on vapor products, and no official figure gives their share of tobacco sales (tax.ny.gov).
Cigarettes also carry excise taxes of $5.35 a pack (state) and $1.50 more in New York City, left out as excise taxes are everywhere.

Hotel stays pay the state and local sales tax plus local occupancy taxes (New York City 5.875% plus up to $2 a room a night and a $1.50 state unit fee; Nassau County 3%; Erie County 5% at hotels of more than 30 rooms), which are not counted here (Publication 848; NYC Department of Finance; county pages).
gaps: Clothing and footwear under $110 an item are exempt from the 4% state tax everywhere, and from local tax too in New York City and Chautauqua, Chenango (outside Norwich), Columbia, Delaware, Dutchess, Greene, Hamilton, Monroe, Putnam and Tioga counties; Norwich taxes them at 1.5% (Publication 718-C). Items of $110 or more are taxed in full, which is not counted here.
New York City taxes barber, beauty, nail, massage, tanning, tattoo and similar services at 4.5% (city tax only, no state tax); they are not taxed elsewhere in the state (Tax Bulletin TB-ST-575).

Gasoline carries the state tax at 8 cents a gallon (8.75 in the MCTD) and each county's or city's own rate on motor fuel, a percentage or, in Chemung, Dutchess, Orange, Oswego (outside the city), Putnam, Rockland and Seneca counties, cents a gallon (Publication 718-F, effective September 1, 2026). Cents are shown as a share of an average New York pump price of $4.49 a gallon (EIA, all grades, September 21 to October 26, 2026), so the gasoline rate moves with the price. Chemung, Dutchess and Oswego's cents-per-gallon elections run through November 30, 2026, and Orange and Rockland's through February 28, 2027.
Rates are by county and by the cities that levy their own tax; towns and villages inside a county take the county rate.
Publication 718 (effective March 1, 2025) was the current edition when downloaded in October 2026.
The 3/8% MCTD tax is included in the combined rate of the 12 MCTD jurisdictions; it is a state-administered tax for the MTA, counted here as local.

programs: Downtown Revitalization Initiative and NY Forward areas are shown through DRI Round 8 and NY Forward Round 3, as the Department of State maps them (June 2026). The 2026 rounds aren't mapped yet: DRI Round 9 went to Rensselaer, Cazenovia, Batavia, Valley Stream, Yonkers, Rome, East Williamsburg, Ogdensburg, Ithaca and Jamestown (ny.gov), and NY Forward's fourth round was announced region by region in 2026. Business improvement districts outside New York City are shown only for Albany (a county map from 2023) and Ithaca; no map was found for those of Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse or other cities.

warn: Stony Brook University's residents are students in its residence halls, which the Census counts as group quarters, not households, so there is no resident spending to show here.

The 2020 census counted 20 people on the Oil Springs Reservation, but the American Community Survey (2020–2024) estimates no households in the census tracts its page is built from, so there is no resident spending to show here.

warn.text: Salamanca draws many visitors (the Seneca Allegany Resort and Casino), but it isn't flagged as a visitor economy over the city as a whole: {visitor_why}. The site's lodging jobs come from Census business counts by county and ZIP code, which can miss or misplace a resort (a ZIP code with fewer than 3 lodging businesses has no row), so they likely read low here. Visitors' spending is part of its local sales, so its retention rates likely overstate how much of residents' own spending stays local.
